Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Dedicated / VPC — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Jordan — great to connect earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Key notes from the call:
- Priority: reduce per-token inference cost on high-volume routes while keeping sub-200ms 95th percentile latency for customer-facing flows.
- Drivers: regulatory requirement to host inference in a VPC / private subnet for certain payment data, and procurement preference for reserved capacity for predictable pricing.
- Current infra: using multi-cloud APIs but looking to move sensitive flows into a private environment.

Suggested path forward:
1) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) deployed into Acme VPC — allows private network connectivity and customer-managed routing (we can provide VPC endpoints + peering options).
2) Initial pilot: 2 gpus with 16GB NVMe-backed caching for 30 days to validate latency and cost.
3) Security checklist: we’ll provide SOC2 evidence, network diagrams, and KMS integration notes (attached).

Requested action items for Acme:
- Confirm whether procurement wants a formal SOW or a one-page order form for reserved capacity.
- Priority/timing: are you targeting a September pilot or later?
- Any additional compliance evidence needed up front (standalone SOC2 attestation vs full audit materials)?

Attachments: redwood_vpc-arch-diagram.pdf, proposal-acme-20260801.pdf

I’m looping in Vivek (our solutions engineer) for the VPC/network details — Vivek, happy to coordinate a short technical call next week.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Appreciate the quick reply, Jordan.

Quick answers:
- Cost: Rough estimate for the 2-GPU pilot in Dedicated (VPC-connected) vs hosted: approximately +$9k–$12k/month over hosted, primarily driven by reserved GPU capacity and dedicated network egress assumptions. I’ve called this out more precisely in the attached proposal (proposal-acme-20260801.pdf). We can tighten the number after we confirm typical token volume and caching profile.
- Networking: no hard blockers — we support VPC peering, PrivateLink-style endpoints, and customer-managed NAT. For a Sept pilot we’ll need: (a) a CIDR for the endpoint, (b) a list of allowed IPs for the peering, and (c) a short IPR (networking) call to finalize routing. Vivek can run that call — Vivek, can you suggest 30-minute slots next week?

Next steps I’ll take: prepare a one-page order form + a draft SOW (attached). If procurement prefers, we can push a DocuSign-ready order form instead of a full SOW to get pilot started quickly.

If I don’t hear back on timing by EOD Friday we’ll assume late-September kickoff.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Jordan — just wanted to bump this thread. I know things get busy; checking in to see if Acme still plans to pilot Dedicated in the VPC. A couple options depending on priority:

1) Pilot in Sept (on schedule) — we’ll lock order form and schedule a 30-min networking sync (Vivek).
2) Push pilot to late Oct / early Nov — we can hold the pricing and pre-approved capacity for 30 days.
3) If priority has changed, happy to pause and revisit later; if so, any feedback that would help us time outreach would be great.

If it helps, I can put together a short 1-page comparison (hosted vs dedicated/VPC) tailored to your token volumes to share with procurement.
